newsitem.title: DUBAI: Oman aims for one million bpd oil output -minister.
newsitem.headline: Oman aims for one million bpd oil output -minister.

text.p: Oman's oil output has hit 900,000 barrels per day (bpd) and may reach one million bpd with the development of a new reservoir zone, Oman Minister of Petroleum and Minerals Said Bin Ahmed Al Shanfari said over the weekend.
Shanfari also said that the Gulf sultanate would shortly award an additional exploration block to accelerate the search for oil in the non-OPEC state.

"The current oil production of the country has reached 900,000 bpd for this year and it is going to be sustained at this level for the next years 1997-2000," Shanfari said in written answers to questions from Reuters.
"In September 1996 the total production of the country had reached 900,000 bpd. The long-term production outlook is promising," Shanfari said.
Oil production averaged 852,000 bpd in 1995, accounting for 76.4 percent of government revenue, according to figures compiled by Oman's Ministry of Development.
The oil ministry's plans to lift crude output by another 11 percent rests on the development of the "Athel" reservoir.
"We hope that the recent discovery of the deep Athel play which has significant potential will contribute to our future production," Shanfari said in his statement.
"A number of technical challenges have to be resolved before this contribution would be realised. That will enable us to produce a million barrels a day," the minister said.

The Athel reservoir is in southern Oman and is close to the major onshore Marmul and Birba crude fields which are operated by the sultanate's largest oil operator Petroleum Development Oman (PDO), oil industry sources said on Sunday.
The high-pressure reservoir is estimated to contain high quality light crude oil, natural gas liquids and gas.
A new exploration licence will also be awarded.
"Four new concessions have been awarded recently and shortly we will award another concession," the minister announced.
Oman's petroleum ministry awarded four exploration blocks in June to foreign firms.
Oman is a major source of oil to Asia, particularly Japan, and its crude is used, especially by Gulf exporters, as a pricing benchmark for sales to east of Suez markets.
